description: This wiki maps crack-related degradation pathways in photovoltaic modules, from the environmental and mechanical stressors that initiate cracking, through the physical mechanisms by which cracks form and propagate, to the structural failures caused by cracking and the resulting electrical and thermal performance losses. The hierarchy follows a four-level chain: stressor → mechanism → failure → performance_loss. Source material is drawn from 50 academic papers and reports on PV module degradation, stored as structured JSON records in the source folder. Of the 50 sources, eight contributed crack-relevant content spanning thin-film delamination, solder joint fatigue, edge seal cracking, glass and silicon cell fracture, adhesive joint cracking, TiO2 coating cracks, and aluminum barrier micro-cracking.
disclaimer: Most source files in this dataset focus on perovskite, CIGS, or organic solar cell chemistry rather than mechanical crack degradation. Only 8 of 50 sources contributed crack-relevant content. The wiki reflects what is documented in the available sources and does not claim comprehensive coverage of all crack degradation mechanisms in PV modules.
